newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin to have heart surgery.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin to have heart surgery.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin, speaking slowly in a television interview, told Russians on Thursday he had agreed to undergo heart surgery, probably at the end of the month in Moscow.
The announcement on NTV commercial television news ended the embarrassed equivocations of aides who for more than two months have been insisting his absence was due only to fatigue.
"I want to have a society based on truth here, that means no longer hiding what we used to hide," The 65-year-old Russian leader said.
"I have undergone routine checks and during these checks they have found something wrong with my heart. Recommendations of doctors, our doctors, were for an operation or to work in a passive way."
Yeltsin, re-elected for a second four-year term in July, said he chose the operation because he could not agree to slow the pace of his work.
He said the operation was likely to take place in late September in an elite Moscow Cardiological centre, one of Russia's leading international medical centres.

"I do not want to go anywhere abroad," he said, in apparent allusion to earlier speculation he might go abroad for surgery. "Our cardiological centre in Moscow is capable of performing such heart operations."
Yeltsin, who effectively presided over the destruction of communist power in the early nineties, had two heart attacks last year.
A Kremlin source told Reuters Yeltsin's operation was likely to be bypass surgery, in which artificial tubes are inserted to replace clogged arteries to improve blood supply to the heart.
Bypass patients can return to active working lives within a month or so of surgery and can go on to live for many years.
Yeltsin disappeared from view shortly before winning a second term on July 3. He has made only public appearance since, looking and sounding stiff at his inauguration on August 9.
Aides had denied speculation he was ill and rumours, especially in financial markets, that he might even be dead.

They insisted the president was simply exhausted after a gruelling election campaign in which he fended off a strong communist challenge with an energetic meet-the-people campaign under the now somewhat ironic slogan "Vote with Your Heart!".

His absence has sparked speculation on power struggles in the Kremlin, with Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, who would take power temporarily if Yeltsin were unable to rule, and security chief Alexander Lebed seen as rivals in the contest.
Russian stock prices fell sharply on news of his surgery.
Yeltsin's chief of staff, Anatoly Chubais, is seen by some observers as governing in Yeltsin's absence.
